description: Verified exam notes for 19 November 2026 covering EPFO reforms, India’s external partnerships, regulatory drafts, water governance, digital public infrastructure, manufacturing, fisheries and urban livelihoods.

stories.title: EPFO board approves voluntary systematic withdrawals and relaxes final-withdrawal safeguards
stories.summary: At its 240th meeting, the Central Board of Trustees of the Employees’ Provident Fund approved a proposal for a voluntary Systematic Withdrawal Plan that would let retiring members receive periodic instalments while the remaining corpus continues to earn returns. The Board also approved reducing the minimum balance requirement from 25% to 10% and the waiting period for final withdrawal from 12 months to two months. The SWP and associated changes still require the necessary scheme amendments and Ministry approval before notification; they are not yet an operational entitlement.
key_facts: The proposed SWP would offer monthly, quarterly or half-yearly withdrawals at the member’s choice.
About 6.32 lakh EPF members aged above 55 with accumulations exceeding ₹5 lakh are expected to be the initial potential beneficiaries.
The Board also gave in-principle approval for investing up to 3% of fresh accretions in eligible alternative investment funds within the existing overall ceiling.
stories.exam_link: Revise the roles of EPFO, the tripartite Central Board of Trustees, and the three major schemes: EPF, EPS and EDLI.
stories.source_title: PIB, Ministry of Labour & Employment — 240th CBT meeting, 19 November 2026

stories.title: Fourth India–Japan 2+2 dialogue expands defence and strategic cooperation
stories.summary: The foreign and defence ministers of India and Japan held the fourth 2+2 Ministerial Meeting in Tokyo. They welcomed a Letter of Intent under which Japan Self-Defense Forces would use Indian firing ranges for their first live-fire training in India, including training involving surface-to-ship missiles. The joint statement also backed closer exercises, defence-industrial cooperation, a rules-based Indo-Pacific and mutual support for permanent membership in a reformed UN Security Council.
key_facts: The 2+2 format brings together the foreign and defence ministers of both countries.
India and Japan agreed to accelerate arrangements for the firing-range initiative; the statement records intent, not completion of the training.
The countries will mark 75 years of diplomatic relations in 2027 as the India–Japan Year of Shared Horizons.
stories.exam_link: Link the development to the India–Japan Special Strategic and Global Partnership, Indo-Pacific cooperation and the structure of 2+2 dialogues.
stories.source_title: PIB joint statement — Fourth India–Japan 2+2 Ministerial Meeting, 19 November 2026

stories.title: India and Italy reaffirm €20 billion bilateral-trade target for 2029
stories.summary: India’s Commerce and Industry Minister and Italy’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister co-chaired the 23rd India–Italy Joint Commission for Economic Cooperation in Rome on 18 November; PIB released the outcome on 19 November. The two sides reviewed trade, investment and industrial cooperation and reaffirmed their shared target of €20 billion in bilateral trade by 2029. Around 80 Indian business delegates, including 12 startups, also participated in the Business and Innovation Forum.
key_facts: The JCEC is the main bilateral institutional mechanism for reviewing India–Italy economic and commercial cooperation.
Cooperation discussions covered trade diversification, investment, manufacturing and technology partnerships.
India and Italy are implementing the Joint Strategic Action Plan 2025–29.
stories.exam_link: Revise India–Italy relations, Italy’s position in the European Union and the function of bilateral joint economic commissions.
stories.source_title: PIB, Ministry of Commerce & Industry — 23rd India–Italy JCEC, 19 November 2026

stories.title: Draft rules propose central regulatory oversight for antimicrobials
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry proposed adding antimicrobials to the definition of a ‘New Drug’ under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 through draft notification G.S.R. 983(E). If finalised, manufacturers would need permission from the Central Licensing Authority before seeking a manufacturing licence from the State Licensing Authority. The draft invites public objections and suggestions and therefore must not be treated as an enacted rule.
key_facts: The proposal would amend Rule 2(1)(w)(v) of the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019.
The stated objective is stronger scrutiny of quality, safety and efficacy, including studies such as bioavailability, bioequivalence and stability studies.
The measure is linked to combating antimicrobial resistance through better regulatory oversight.
stories.exam_link: Connect the proposal with antimicrobial resistance, the One Health approach, and the division of drug-licensing functions between central and state authorities.
stories.source_title: PIB, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare — draft antimicrobial amendment, 19 November 2026

stories.title: MoRTH proposes age- and emission-standard-based PUC certificate validity
stories.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways proposed amending Rule 115(7) to vary Pollution Under Control certificate validity according to Bharat Stage emission standard, vehicle category and age. The draft would retain shorter intervals for older or earlier-standard vehicles while allowing longer validity for newer BS-VI vehicles. These periods are proposals and will apply only after the amendment comes into force, with transitional treatment for existing certificates.
key_facts: The proposed validity is three months for BS-I to BS-III vehicles and six months for BS-IV vehicles.
For BS-VI non-transport vehicles, the proposal is three years up to age six, one year from over six to ten years, and six months above ten years.
For BS-VI transport vehicles, the proposed initial validity is two years up to age six, followed by one year and then six months in the older age bands.
stories.exam_link: Revise Bharat Stage emission norms, in-use vehicle emission testing and the Central Motor Vehicles Rules framework.
stories.source_title: PIB, Ministry of Road Transport & Highways — proposed PUC validity revision, 19 November 2026

stories.title: BHASHINI highlights voice-first multilingual AI for public digital services
stories.summary: The Digital India BHASHINI Division showcased voice-first and multilingual artificial-intelligence applications at Dakshin Day 2026, a policy dialogue on South–South cooperation. The platform demonstrated language technologies for digital governance, public-service delivery and citizen engagement. BHASHINI is housed in the Digital India Corporation under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and forms part of India’s language-technology digital public infrastructure.
key_facts: The official release states that BHASHINI supports 36 Indian text languages and 23 Indian voice languages.
It also supports 35 international languages for integration into government and public-facing services.
Dakshin Day 2026 was organised by RIS with the Ministry of External Affairs at the India Habitat Centre, New Delhi.
stories.exam_link: Revise the National Language Translation Mission, Digital India Corporation and the role of multilingual AI in inclusive digital public infrastructure.
stories.source_title: PIB, Ministry of Electronics & IT — BHASHINI at Dakshin 2026, 19 November 2026

stories.title: Letters of Intent issued to 25 firms for Gwalior Telecom Manufacturing Zone
stories.summary: The Department of Telecommunications and the Madhya Pradesh government distributed Letters of Intent to 25 companies proposing investments in the Telecom Manufacturing Zone at Gwalior. The programme also announced Phase II of the zone. The initiative is envisaged as an integrated cluster for telecom manufacturing, research, development and innovation; the LoIs indicate planned investment participation rather than completed factories or production.
key_facts: The Madhya Pradesh Cabinet has approved about 170 acres of land for the zone.
Planned activities include telecom equipment, components, optical fibre, software and passive infrastructure.
The zone is a Centre–State collaboration involving the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh.
stories.exam_link: Connect industrial clusters with domestic telecom manufacturing, supply-chain resilience and the respective roles of Union and state governments in industrial promotion.
stories.source_title: PIB, Ministry of Communications — Gwalior Telecom Manufacturing Zone LoIs, 19 November 2026

stories.title: Four districts present service-delivery models at Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 dialogue
stories.summary: The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation held the 14th District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad to share district-level practices for Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. Presentations focused on community ownership, operation and maintenance, source sustainability, skills and continuous rural water supply. Officials also urged regular District Water and Sanitation Committee meetings, data-based planning through the Decision Support System and district improvement plans after Jal Seva Aankalan.
key_facts: The four presenting districts were from Himachal Pradesh, Gujarat, Assam and Tripura.
The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation functions under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
The Samvad is a knowledge-sharing platform; it is not itself a new funding scheme or a declaration of universal completion.
stories.exam_link: Revise Jal Jeevan Mission, the Har Ghar Jal objective, local water-service operation and maintenance, and district-level convergence institutions.
stories.source_title: PIB, Ministry of Jal Shakti — 14th District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad, 19 November 2026

stories.title: Fourteenth fisheries forum links frontier science with sustainable aquaculture
stories.summary: The 14th Indian Fisheries and Aquaculture Forum convened at ICAR–Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture in Bhubaneswar for 18–20 November. More than 1,000 participants from India and six other countries joined discussions on sustainable fisheries, aquatic ecosystems and technology-led aquaculture. The event’s theme is ‘Transforming Aquaculture and Fisheries: Bridging Science and Society’.
key_facts: The forum is jointly organised by bodies including the Asian Fisheries Society Indian Branch, ICAR-CIFA, the Department of Fisheries and the National Fisheries Development Board.
Technical areas include artificial intelligence, genome editing, precision aquaculture, breeding, feed, aquatic animal health and genetic improvement.
A concurrent exhibition features 20 agencies showcasing fisheries and aquaculture technologies.
stories.exam_link: Revise ICAR’s research network, the role of ICAR-CIFA and NFDB, and the distinction between capture fisheries and aquaculture.
stories.source_title: PIB, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare — 14th Indian Fisheries and Aquaculture Forum, 19 November 2026

stories.title: CSIR-TKDL and Indian Knowledge Systems Division renew collaboration on traditional knowledge
stories.summary: The CSIR–Traditional Knowledge Digital Library Unit and the Indian Knowledge Systems Division of the Ministry of Education signed an MoU to deepen work on traditional knowledge, intellectual-property rights and the rights of knowledge holders. The agreement builds on their 2023 collaboration and envisages education, research, awareness and guidance on patents, copyrights, geographical indications, attribution and equitable benefit-sharing.
key_facts: The earlier collaboration conducted 11 workshops for participants including students, researchers, faculty, scientists and Army personnel.
TKDL helps document Indian traditional knowledge so that patent examiners can identify prior art and prevent erroneous patents.
The renewed partnership emphasises protection and responsible contemporary use rather than treating all traditional knowledge as freely appropriable.
stories.exam_link: Revise prior art, patents, geographical indications, benefit-sharing and the defensive-protection role of the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library.
stories.source_title: PIB, Ministry of Science & Technology — CSIR-TKDL and IKS Division MoU, 19 November 2026

stories.title: India schedules first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi
stories.summary: The Prime Minister’s Office announced that India would host the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila, New Delhi, from 20 to 22 November. The forum is intended to connect scholars and cultural representatives around shared civilisational heritage and people-to-people ties. Because the event was scheduled for the following day, this item records an official plan rather than a completed inauguration.
key_facts: The initiative follows India’s proposal at the 2025 SCO Summit in Tianjin, later welcomed in the Bishkek Declaration.
Planned sessions cover performing arts, textiles, cuisine, traditional games, architecture, scripts, manuscripts, monastic trails and philosophy.
The venue is Purana Qila, and the cultural theme is Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam.
stories.exam_link: Revise the SCO’s Eurasian focus, India’s membership, and the organisation’s use of cultural and people-to-people cooperation alongside security and economic agendas.
stories.source_title: PIB, Prime Minister’s Office — first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum announcement, 19 November 2026

stories.title: PM SVANidhi awards announcement highlights expansion of street-vendor credit
stories.summary: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs announced that the SVANidhi Samman Awards would be held on 20 November to recognise states, urban local bodies, lenders and partners supporting street vendors. Its same-day scheme brief reported that PM SVANidhi had enabled about 81 lakh vendors to access more than 1.21 crore loans worth roughly ₹20,000 crore since June 2020. The awards were still forthcoming, while the loan data and the 2025 restructuring were completed developments.
key_facts: The restructured scheme was extended to March 2030 and expanded beyond statutory towns to Census Towns and peri-urban areas.
Eligible beneficiaries who repay the second tranche may receive a UPI-linked RuPay credit card with a limit of up to ₹30,000.
SVANidhi se Samriddhi links beneficiary families with other central welfare schemes through socio-economic profiling.
stories.exam_link: Revise urban informal livelihoods, working-capital credit, financial inclusion, urban local bodies and the Street Vendors Act, 2014.
stories.source_title: PIB, Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs — PM SVANidhi Samman Awards announcement, 19 November 2026

mcqs.question: Which body approved the proposal for a voluntary Systematic Withdrawal Plan for EPF members?
options: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
mcqs.explanation: The tripartite Central Board of Trustees of the Employees’ Provident Fund approved the proposal at its 240th meeting.

mcqs.question: Under the EPFO Board’s 19 November decision, the proposed minimum EPF balance requirement would be reduced to what level?
mcqs.explanation: The Board approved reducing the minimum balance requirement from 25% to 10%, subject to the required implementation steps.

mcqs.question: The India–Japan Letter of Intent discussed at the fourth 2+2 meeting principally concerns which activity?
options: Joint operation of a civilian airport
Japan’s use of Indian firing ranges for live-fire training
mcqs.explanation: The LoI concerns use of Indian firing ranges by Japan Self-Defense Forces, including planned surface-to-ship missile training.

mcqs.question: India and Italy reaffirmed a bilateral-trade target of €20 billion by which year?
mcqs.explanation: The 23rd JCEC reaffirmed the shared target of €20 billion in bilateral trade by 2029.

mcqs.question: If the draft antimicrobial amendment is finalised, which authority’s permission would precede a state manufacturing-licence application?
options: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
mcqs.explanation: Manufacturers would first require permission from the Central Licensing Authority before applying to the State Licensing Authority.

mcqs.question: What PUC validity is proposed for BS-IV vehicles under the MoRTH amendment?
mcqs.explanation: The proposal sets a six-month validity for BS-IV vehicles, while BS-I to BS-III vehicles would have three months.

mcqs.question: BHASHINI is institutionally located under which Union ministry?
options: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
mcqs.explanation: The Digital India BHASHINI Division is housed in Digital India Corporation under MeitY.

mcqs.question: According to the 19 November official release, BHASHINI supports how many Indian voice languages?
mcqs.explanation: The release lists 23 Indian voice languages, 36 Indian text languages and 35 international languages.

mcqs.question: The Telecom Manufacturing Zone receiving LoIs from 25 firms is planned at which city?
mcqs.explanation: The planned integrated telecom manufacturing cluster is at Gwalior in Madhya Pradesh.

mcqs.question: The District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad is associated with which mission?
mcqs.explanation: The 14th Samvad shared district practices for sustainable rural water service delivery under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.

mcqs.question: ICAR-CIFA, host of the 14th Indian Fisheries and Aquaculture Forum, is headquartered in which city?
mcqs.explanation: The Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture is based in Bhubaneswar, Odisha.

mcqs.question: Which of the following was specifically listed as a frontier topic at the fisheries forum?
mcqs.explanation: The forum’s technical agenda included genome editing, AI, precision aquaculture, breeding and aquatic animal health.

mcqs.question: What is the primary defensive intellectual-property role of the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library?
options: Documenting prior art to prevent erroneous patents
mcqs.explanation: TKDL makes documented traditional knowledge available as prior art so patent examiners can reject claims that are not genuinely novel.

mcqs.question: The first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum was scheduled at which New Delhi site?
mcqs.explanation: The PMO announcement scheduled the forum at Purana Qila from 20 to 22 November 2026.

mcqs.question: PM SVANidhi primarily provides what type of support to eligible street vendors?
mcqs.explanation: PM SVANidhi is designed around working-capital loans and related financial-inclusion support for street vendors.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the legal status of the antimicrobial and PUC developments in this edition?
options: Both are final rules already in force
Both are draft proposals awaiting finalisation
Only the antimicrobial measure is final
Only the PUC measure is final
mcqs.explanation: Both releases describe proposed amendments; neither should be presented as a final operational rule.
